coding.description: Architecture, supervision, and delivery; direct work or delegation by judgment

models.guidance: Preferred main coding model, routed through the Subs Claude pool (CLIProxyAPI); the direct anthropic provider is not part of routing, so never retry Opus through it. Configured default for general, including all implementation (UI included) in public or private repositories; implementation fallback chain is subs-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, then xai/grok-4.7, then zai/glm-5.3. Also the configured default for pr-reviewer, for tech-lead (fallback: Astra, then public-only Muse, nothing else), and for ui-design in either public or private repositories. For ui-design: design direction, interaction specifications, and implementation guidelines, not routine UI implementation. UI implementation belongs to general following accepted design guidelines. In the PR skill, Opus is the primary independent opinion and Astra the secondary one, both reviewing the same patch and criteria when available. Also the configured default for aha (thinking medium): one Aha page per launch, public or private content; brief it with the content request only, since the agent prompt carries the Aha workflow and guardrails.

Via the Subs gateway; second independent pr-reviewer opinion after Opus 5.5 and first tech-lead fallback after Opus 5.5. The configured models do not have overlapping provider routes, so never retry the same model through another provider. Explicit user provider/model selection determines the initial model; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact model or forbids fallback. On model availability, authentication, or quota failure, inspect any partial work and automatically continue through the configured model chain using a new explicit pi-subagents launch without waiting for confirmation. Report the exact failed model, reason, and fallback model so the transition is observable. Unrelated launch/tooling/workflow failures remain infrastructure blockers under pi-subagents recovery rules. Tech-lead automatic chain: Opus 5.5 (default), then Astra, then public-only Muse; no other fallback, and if none is eligible report the checkpoint as blocked. The PR skill requests independent opinions from both subs-claude/claude-opus-5-5 (primary, the pr-reviewer default) and Astra (secondary, explicit per-launch override) on the same patch and criteria when available. Use tech-lead for frontier judgment checkpoints (architecture, difficult tradeoffs, contested decisions) when the main session needs an independent frontier opinion. Main-model selection remains independent of identity activation.

Default for explore-codebase in verified public repositories (explicit per-launch override) and the final public-only tech-lead fallback. Not used for implementation by default. Verify the actual repository is public and the handoff contains no private material before using Muse by default; a remote URL alone is not evidence of public visibility. Never send private or unknown-visibility repository context to Muse by default. An explicit user instruction to use Muse overrides this default routing regardless of repository visibility; confirm the requested scope and proceed with the user's choice.

First automatic fallback from subs-claude/claude-opus-5-5 for general and all implementation (including UI implementation), in public or private repositories. If Sol is unavailable, authentication fails, or quota is exhausted, inspect any partial work and automatically continue with xai/grok-4.7; if Grok also fails, continue with zai/glm-5.3. Report each failed model and selected fallback. Unrelated launch/tooling/workflow failures remain infrastructure blockers and must not trigger this model fallback chain or an execution-engine change. For UI implementation, follow accepted design guidelines. An explicit user instruction to use another model determines the initial model; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact route or forbids fallback.

Second automatic fallback for general and implementation, after subs-claude/claude-opus-5-5 and subs-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, including private or unknown-visibility repository work. If Grok is unavailable, authentication fails, or quota is exhausted, continue with zai/glm-5.3 as the final fallback. Inspect any partial work before switching models, report the failed model and selected fallback, and do not retry through another provider route. Explicit user provider/model selection determines the initial model; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact route or forbids fallback.

Final automatic fallback for general and implementation (including UI implementation), after subs-claude/claude-opus-5-5, subs-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, and xai/grok-4.7. Inspect any partial work before switching, report the failed model and selected fallback, and do not retry Opus, Sol, Grok, or GLM through another provider. Unrelated launch/tooling/workflow failures remain infrastructure blockers and must not trigger this fallback or an execution-engine change. For UI implementation, follow accepted design guidelines. An explicit user instruction to use another model determines the initial model; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact route or forbids fallback.

Configured default for explore-codebase in private or unknown-visibility repositories, and for web-researcher regardless of repository visibility. For explore-codebase in verified public repositories, explicitly select Muse instead. An explicit user instruction to use Muse overrides visibility routing.
